diagnostic_evidence.quote: We call $P$ a \textit{$(t,\bse,m,d)$-net in base $b$} if every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $(b^{e_1},\dots,b^{e_d})$ with $e_1k_1 + \cdots + e_dk_d \le m-t$ contains exactly $b^t$ points of $P$.
the notion of a $(0,\bse,d)$-sequence in base $b$ is identical to that of an equidistributed sequence in base $(b^{e_1}, \dots, b^{e_d})$.

issues.failure_explanation: As stated, the whole space $[0,1)^d$ (the elementary $(0,\dots,0)$-interval, whose exponent sum $0\le m-t$) would have to contain exactly $b^t$ points, but $P$ has $b^m$ points; hence for $t<m$ no such point set exists and the definition is vacuous (it even excludes the standard 4-point $(0,2,1)$-net $\{0,1/4,1/2,3/4\}$ in base 2, since $[0,1)$ contains 4 rather than 1 point). The standard definition requires every elementary interval with $\sum_j k_j = m-t$ (equivalently volume $b^{t-m}$) to contain exactly $b^t$ points, i.e. intervals with $\sum_j k_j\le m-t$ contain exactly $b^{m-\sum_j k_j}$ points. Under the standard definition the paper's identity claim ($(0,\bse,d)$-sequences are exactly equidistributed sequences in base $(b^{e_j})$) and the cited thm:t-val-nied and thm:added-1 hold; under the literal displayed definition they are false.

failure_location.quote: We call $P$ a \textit{$(t,m,d)$-net in base $b$} if every elementary $(k_1, \dots, k_d)$-interval in base $(b,\dots,b)$ with $k_1 + \cdots + k_d \le m-t$ contains exactly $b^t$ points of $P$.

issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Correct both net definitions to the standard one: every elementary interval with $\sum_j k_j = m-t$ (equivalently volume $b^{t-m}$) contains exactly $b^t$ points, i.e. intervals with $\sum_j k_j\le m-t$ contain exactly $b^{m-\sum_j k_j}$ points. No other change is needed.
issues.overall_effect: The definitions of $(t,m,d)$-nets, $(t,d)$-sequences, $(t,\bse,m,d)$-nets and $(0,\bse,d)$-sequences are literally false (vacuous) as displayed, so the paper's central objects and the statements of thm:t-val-nied and thm:added-1 are unreliable as written; all subsequent results are consistent only with the standard definition that the source forces.
issues.title: Vacuous definition of (t,m,d)-nets and (t,e,m,d)-nets (wrong point count)
issues.why_classification: A one-line correction to the standard definition restores every statement; no proof, rate, or advertised scope is lost, so the issue is minor.

diagnostic_evidence.quote: C_{u,v,\bsk}(P_n) = \frac{1}{n^2} \sum_{i=0}^{n-1}\sum_{i'=0}^{n-1} \chi(\text{$\bsx_i$ and $\bsx_{i'}$ are in the same elementary $(\bsk + \bsone_v)$-interval}).

issues.failure_explanation: Expanding the product in eq:Gtilda_def gives $\widetilde G=\frac1n\sum_vH_{u,v}\cdot[\text{unnormalized pair count}]$; with eq:C_def's $1/n^2$ normalization this reads $\widetilde G=n\sum_vH_{u,v}C_{u,v,\bsk}$, contradicting eq:Gtilda_formula ($\widetilde G=\sum_vH_{u,v}C_{u,v,\bsk}$). Similarly eq:Cformula and the proof of lem:Cformula compute the unnormalized count, contradicting eq:C_def's $1/n^2$: for $n=m_{u,v,\bsk}$ (one full block of an equidistributed sequence) eq:Cformula gives $C=n$ while eq:C_def gives $C=1/n$. Hence $G=\frac1n\prod(b_j-1)^{-1}\widetilde G$ as literally defined in def:gain is too small by a factor $n$: e.g. for the 2-point van der Corput sequence and $f(x)=x$ it yields $G_{\{1\},k}(2)=1/2$ ($k\ge1$), while the exact variance $1/96=\frac12\sum_{k\ge1}\sigma^2_k$ forces $G_{\{1\},k}(2)=1$. All proofs use the consistent chain eq:G_Gtilde + eq:Gtilda_formula + eq:Cformula (matching Owen's theory), so no theorem is invalidated; only the two defining displays are wrong.
issues.least_adequate_overall_repair: Remove the spurious factor $1/n$ in eq:Gtilda_def and $1/n^2$ in eq:C_def (define $\widetilde G$ and $C$ as unnormalized sums). Then eq:Gtilda_formula, eq:Cformula, eq:G_Gtilde, lem:Cformula and thm:added-2 are mutually consistent and correct, with no change to any proof or result.
issues.overall_effect: The displayed definitions of $C_{u,v,\bsk}$ (eq:C_def) and $\widetilde G_{u,\bsk}$ (eq:Gtilda_def), and hence of $G_{u,\bsk}$ as literally defined in def:gain, are mutually inconsistent and inconsistent with the variance formula thm:added-2; taken literally the gain coefficients are too small by a factor $n$. Every proved result uses the consistent correct chain, so no formal result is invalidated; the defect is confined to the two defining displays and the proof-citation in lem:Cformula.
issues.title: Inconsistent normalization in the definitions of the gain-coefficient components
issues.why_classification: The repair is a two-factor normalization fix in the defining displays; it needs no new lemma or argument and preserves every theorem and guarantee, since all proofs already use the correct normalization, so the issue is minor.
